summary: Unpredictable single insert performance in SQL Server due to blocking behavior and excessive indexes.
symptoms: Single record insert takes several minutes.
Blocking session IDs appear in sys.dm_exec_requests but the blocker session is not active.
Wait type observed is LCK_M_S (shared lock).
mechanism: Blocking caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks, exacerbated by excessive indexes.

facts.evidence: The post mentions blocked sessions with session IDs that appear inactive.
The post explicitly mentions LCK_M_S as the wait type.
The post mentions the table has 34 indexes despite being in an OLTP system.

assumptions: The blocking behavior is caused by uncommitted transactions holding locks.
Excessive indexes contribute to the poor insert performance.
unknowns: Exact schema of the table and indexes.
Whether the blocking sessions are caused by application behavior or SQL Server configuration.
